# Method and source

This analysis uses the Hungarian fastText word vectors (`cc.hu.300.vec.gz`, 300 dimensions), trained on Common Crawl and Wikipedia.

[Model documentation and downloads](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/crawl-vectors.html).
The vectors are distributed under CC BY-SA 3.0.

Reference: 
Grave, E., Bojanowski, P., Gupta, P., Joulin, A., & Mikolov, T.(2018).[Learning Word Vectors for 157 Languages](https://aclanthology.org/L18-1550/).In *Proceedings of the Eleventh International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC 2018)*.

The candidate words were assembled for this project using AI suggestions and researcher additions. They are not a normed stimulus set or the SPAML word list.

Cosine similarity describes the alignment of word vectors, not recall difficulty. A value of -1 means opposite vector directions, not opposite meanings. Every unordered combination is calculated once, excluding self-pairs.The 0.15–0.30 interval is a provisional selection criterion. Filtering does not select a final set of non-overlapping pairs.

# Settings

Save this document as UTF-8 and click **Render** in RStudio.
Set the path to the downloaded `.vec.gz` file below; do not unzip it.

```{r}
model_file <- "C:/Users/Acer/Downloads/cc.hu.300.vec.gz"
output_dir <- "wordpair_cosine_results"
cosine_min <- 0.15
cosine_max <- 0.30
```

# Validation of the word list

The code will check that the word list meets the following criteria:

```{r}
if (!isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]])) {
  stop("Use a UTF-8 R session before running this document.")
}
if (length(words) < 2 || anyNA(words) || any(!nzchar(words)) ||
    any(grepl("[[:space:]]", words)) || anyDuplicated(words)) {
  stop("The word list must contain unique, nonempty, single-word entries.")
}
if (any(words %in% practice_words)) {
  stop("Remove practice words from the candidate list.")
}
if (!is.finite(cosine_min) || !is.finite(cosine_max) ||
    cosine_min < -1 || cosine_max > 1 || cosine_min > cosine_max) {
  stop("The cosine limits must satisfy -1 <= minimum <= maximum <= 1.")
}
```

# Read the word vectors

Only vectors for the listed words are retained. The large model file is read in chunks to avoid loading it entirely into memory.

```{r}
read_vectors <- function(path, words) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Model file not found: ", path)
  connection <- gzfile(path, open = "rt")
  on.exit(close(connection))
  header <- scan(connection, what = integer(), nlines = 1, quiet = TRUE)
  if (length(header) != 2 || anyNA(header) ||
      header[1] < 1 || header[2] != 300) {
    stop("Expected the 300-dimensional fastText text-vector file.")
  }
  vectors <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(words), ncol = header[2],
                    dimnames = list(words, NULL))
  found <- rep(FALSE, length(words))
  repeat {
    lines <- readLines(connection, n = 5000, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE)
    if (!length(lines)) break
    tokens <- sub("[ \t].*$", "", lines)
    positions <- match(tokens, words)
    for (i in which(!is.na(positions))) {
      j <- positions[i]
      if (found[j]) next
      values <- scan(text = sub("^[^ \t]+[ \t]+", "", lines[i]),
                     what = double(), quiet = TRUE)
      if (length(values) != ncol(vectors) || any(!is.finite(values))) {
        stop("Invalid vector for: ", words[j])
      }
      vectors[j, ] <- values
      found[j] <- TRUE
    }
    if (all(found)) break
  }
  if (!all(found)) {
    stop("Words missing from the model: ", paste(words[!found], collapse = ", "))
  }
  vectors
}
vectors <- read_vectors(model_file, words)
```

# Calculate and filter

```{r}
norms <- sqrt(rowSums(vectors^2))
if (any(!is.finite(norms) | norms == 0)) stop("Invalid vector length.")
unit_vectors <- sweep(vectors, 1, norms, "/")
similarities <- tcrossprod(unit_vectors)
indices <- t(combn(seq_along(words), 2))
all_pairs <- data.frame(
  word_1 = words[indices[, 1]],
  word_2 = words[indices[, 2]],
  cosine_similarity = pmax(-1, pmin(1, similarities[indices]))
)
all_pairs <- all_pairs[order(-all_pairs$cosine_similarity), ]
rownames(all_pairs) <- NULL
candidates <- subset(
  all_pairs,
  cosine_similarity >= cosine_min & cosine_similarity <= cosine_max
)
```

# Select a non-overlapping pair pool

The aim is to create a pool of 50 pairs from 100 words, using every word
exactly once.

The selection proceeds as follows:

1. **Apply the cosine limits.** Only pairs in the previously created `candidates` table are eligible. These pairs have cosine similarities between `cosine_min` and `cosine_max`, currently 0.15 and 0.30. Within this interval, higher or lower cosine values are not preferred.

2. **Assign random priorities.** Each eligible pair receives a random number between 0 and 1. This number is only a selection priority, not a measure of the pair's quality or learning difficulty.

3. **Find a complete pairing.** The algorithm selects the combination of pairs with the highest total priority, subject to the requirement that every word appears exactly once. It considers the complete pairing, rather than simply taking the 50 highest-priority pairs, which could contain repeated words.

4. **Assign cue and target roles.** For each selected pair, a random decision determines which word will be shown as the cue and which word participants will need to recall.

A fixed random seed makes the selection repeatable: with the same input data, candidate order, and software environment, each run produces the same pairs and cue–target directions.

This procedure does **not** give every possible complete pairing an equal chance of selection. It also does not optimize cosine similarity within the allowed interval or control word frequency, length, emotional valence, or recall difficulty.

```{r}
# Fix the random seed and generator so the random priorities and cue–target assignments can be reproduced on subsequent runs.
selection_seed <- 20261020L
set.seed(selection_seed, kind = "Mersenne-Twister")

# An even number of words is required to use every word exactly once.
if (length(words) %% 2 != 0) {
  stop("The number of words must be even.")
}

# Stop if no pairs passed the cosine filter.
if (nrow(candidates) == 0) {
  stop("There are no eligible candidate pairs.")
}

# Build a word-by-pair membership matrix: each row represents one word; each column represents one eligible pair; TRUE means that the word occurs in that pair.
incidence <- outer(words, candidates$word_1, "==") |
             outer(words, candidates$word_2, "==")

# Give each eligible pair a random selection priority. These priorities are independent of the pairs' cosine values.
pair_priorities <- runif(nrow(candidates))

# Select pairs using binary optimization. Each pair receives a decision value: 1 = selected, 0 = not selected.
fit <- lpSolve::lp(
  # Maximize the sum of the selected pairs' random priorities.
  direction = "max",
  objective.in = pair_priorities,

  # Convert TRUE/FALSE membership values to 1/0.
  const.mat = incidence * 1L,

  # For every word, the number of selected pairs containing it
  # must equal exactly 1.
  const.dir = rep("=", length(words)),
  const.rhs = rep(1, length(words)),

  # Require each selection decision to be either 0 or 1.
  all.bin = TRUE,

  # Limit the solver's running time to 60 seconds.
  timeout = 60
)

# Status 2 means that the constraints cannot be satisfied: there is no complete pairing using only the eligible pairs.
if (fit$status == 2) {
  stop("No complete pairing is possible within the current cosine interval.")
}

# Other unsuccessful statuses can include reaching the time limit. They do not necessarily mean that a complete pairing is impossible.
if (fit$status != 0) {
  stop(
    "The solver did not finish successfully. Status: ", fit$status,
    ". This does not establish that a complete pairing is impossible."
  )
}

# Keep the selected pairs.
# The threshold accommodates numerical representation of binary decisions.
chosen <- candidates[fit$solution > 0.5, , drop = FALSE]

# Collect both words from every selected pair for verification.
used_words <- c(chosen$word_1, chosen$word_2)

# Verify that: the number of pairs is half the number of words; no word is repeated; every original word is included; every selected pair satisfies the cosine limits.
stopifnot(
  nrow(chosen) == length(words) / 2,
  !anyDuplicated(used_words),
  setequal(used_words, words),
  all(chosen$cosine_similarity >= cosine_min),
  all(chosen$cosine_similarity <= cosine_max)
)

# Decide whether to reverse each pair's original word order.
# Each pair has a 50% chance of being reversed.
# This uses the continuing seeded random sequence, so it is repeatable.
reverse_pair <- runif(nrow(chosen)) < 0.5

# Create the final pool:
# - cue: the word shown during the recall test;
# - target: the word participants should recall.
# Reversing a pair does not change its cosine similarity.
selected_pairs <- data.frame(
  pair_id = sprintf("main_%02d", seq_len(nrow(chosen))),
  cue = ifelse(reverse_pair, chosen$word_2, chosen$word_1),
  target = ifelse(reverse_pair, chosen$word_1, chosen$word_2),
  cosine_similarity = chosen$cosine_similarity,
  selection_seed = selection_seed
)

# Display the complete selected pool in the rendered document.
# Saving it to CSV is handled in the following Save section.
knitr::kable(selected_pairs, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Save

Each run creates a new folder inside `wordpair_cosine_results`, relative to the document's working directory. 
Three CSV files are saved:
- `all_pair_cosines.csv`: all combinations.
- `candidate_pairs.csv`: combinations within the chosen interval.
- `selected_pairs.csv`: the final selected pairs.

```{r}
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

run_dir <- tempfile(pattern = "run_", tmpdir = output_dir)

if (!dir.create(run_dir)) stop("Could not create the output folder.")

write.csv(all_pairs, file.path(run_dir, "all_pair_cosines.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

write.csv(candidates, file.path(run_dir, "candidate_pairs.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

write.csv(selected_pairs, file.path(run_dir, "selected_pairs.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
```
